_: Mud: fine soil (silt/clay) above its plastic limit, near or above the liquid limit, saturated. Strength is the undrained shear strength c_u (phi_u = 0); a foot sinks until the bearing pressure equals 5.14 c_u + gamma z; suction holds the foot on lifting. World lane 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: a wet smooth mud surface: glossy where water stands, matte where it has drained

n.src: the surface is a water film (water n)

albedo_visible.src: dark: saturated fine soil, LEKNER88 (total internal reflection in the water film: more absorption per escaping photon), LOBELL02 (reflectance falls roughly exponentially with water content)

static.src: tan(friction angle): a body sliding on or shearing the ground is limited by the ground's own shear strength (Mohr-Coulomb), not by a surface coefficient; pair values in pairs/world.json

permeability_m2.src: k = K mu/(rho g) from hydraulic conductivity K [1e-10, 1e-07] m/s (FHWA_GEC: clays/silts)

hydraulic_conductivity_m_s.src: FHWA_GEC: E: recalled from FHWA_GEC, not re-read (was M); FHWA_GEC: clays/silts

water_retention.src: saturated: water content = porosity (1 - 1.6/2.7 ~ 0.41 at bulk 1.6; up to ~0.6 for fluid mud)

suction.v: mud sticks to and holds the foot: lifting needs extra force (pore-water suction); mud coats skin and soles

tack.src: not found: a pull-off number for a foot in mud

collision_thickness_mm.src: half the median grain (deform.grain_size_mm d50): the roughness a contact rides on

ramp.v: bekker_power: p = (k_c/b + k_phi) z^n on loading; plastic: the sinkage stays on unloading (elastic rebound a few % of z)

contact_damping_ratio.src: ANON_E: soil/granular contact dissipates most of the energy (plastic flow, grain friction): near-critical damping

bekker_k_c_kN_m_n1.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08 (as deform.bekker)

bekker_k_phi_kN_m_n2.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08

bekker_n.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: tangent dp/dz = n p / z at the standing foot load (p 20 kPa, b 0.09 m, z 2.2 mm) from the Bekker set; small foot on plate parameters: indicative

response_time_ms.src: ANON_E: an impact into a granular bed lasts ~ penetration depth / speed (cm at m/s: ~10 ms); mud longer (viscous squeeze)

wave_speed_m_s.src: shear sqrt(G/rho), G = E/(2(1+nu)) with E 1.6 MPa (mid of deform.E_MPa), nu 0.49, rho 1600; at the free surface the confining stress is ~0 and the real speed is far lower (~50-150 m/s in loose sand, E)

damping_ratio.src: ANON_E: small-strain soil damping 2-10 %, rising with strain (FHWA_GEC trend)

model.src: TERZAGHI / FHWA_GEC: granular and soil strength

density_kg_m3.src: TERZAGHI / FHWA_GEC: saturated soft clays/silts 1.5-1.8 g/cm3

particle_density_kg_m3.src: FHWA_GEC: E: recalled from FHWA_GEC, not re-read (was M); FHWA_GEC: clay minerals 2.65-2.80

friction_angle_deg.src: undrained (phi_u = 0) analysis for saturated mud (TERZAGHI); drained phi of clays 15-25 deg (FHWA_GEC)

cohesion_kPa.src: TERZAGHI consistency: very soft clay c_u < 12 kPa; liquid-limit soils ~1-2 kPa

angle_of_repose_deg.src: fluid mud slumps to near flat; stiff mud stands in clods

E_MPa.src: FHWA_GEC: E: recalled from FHWA_GEC, not re-read (was M); FHWA_GEC very soft clays 0.5-5 MPa (undrained)

n.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08 Table 2.3 clayey soil, Thailand, 55 % moisture

k_c_kN_m_n1.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08 clayey soil, Thailand, 55 % moisture

k_phi_kN_m_n2.src: WONG08: E: recalled from WONG08, not re-read (was M); WONG08 clayey soil, Thailand, 55 % moisture

v.bearing_balance_note: footprint depth where 5.14 c_u + gamma z = p: with c_u 5 kPa and p 20 kPa standing, z ~ (20-25.7)/16 < 0: the foot is carried; at c_u 2 kPa: 20-10.3 = 9.7 kPa / 16 kN/m3 ~ 0.6 m in a single bearing failure, in practice ankle-deep (~0.1-0.2 m) as the mud squeezes out

footprint_sinkage_mm.src: TERZAGHI q_ult = 5.14 c_u; WONG08 Thai clay 55 % for the Bekker value; ankle-deep observation E

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: FAROUKI81: soil minerals ~0.7-0.9 kJ/kgK dry (water raises the bulk value)

emissivity.src: FAROUKI81 / remote-sensing tables (soils and sands 0.90-0.96; wet higher)

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) with the values above

fluid_mud.src: Bingham yield stress of muddy debris/slurries 10-1000 Pa (Coussot-type rheology, recalled; not re-checked)

drying_cracked.src: ANON_E: desiccated clay crust, polygonal cracks

WONG08.cite: Wong JY. Theory of Ground Vehicles, 4th ed. Wiley (2008), Table 2.3 (Bekker pressure-sinkage and Mohr-Coulomb parameters of soils, from Bekker / Land Locomotion Lab / WES). Values recalled as widely reproduced; the LETE sand set is confirmed by the Project Chrono forum post (mail-archive.com projectchrono msg01991)
WONG08.lic: book, copyright; individual parameters used as facts, table not copied in bulk

USDA_NRCS.cite: USDA NRCS Soil Quality Indicators: Bulk Density (2008/2019) and Soil Survey Manual (Handbook 18, 2017): bulk densities by texture, particle density 2.65 g/cm3, texture classes, available water by texture

FHWA_GEC.cite: FHWA Geotechnical Engineering Circulars (GEC 5 Evaluation of Soil and Rock Properties, FHWA-IF-02-034, 2002; GEC 6 Shallow Foundations) and the NAVFAC DM 7.01/7.02 design manuals: friction angles, unit weights, elastic moduli, hydraulic conductivity ranges by soil type. Ranges recalled

IBC18.cite: International Building Code 2018, Table 1806.2 presumptive load-bearing values (sandy gravel 3000 psf; sand, silty sand 2000 psf; clay, silt 1500 psf)
IBC18.lic: ICC copyright; three code values used as facts

TERZAGHI.cite: Terzaghi K, Peck RB, Mesri G. Soil Mechanics in Engineering Practice, 3rd ed. (1996): bearing capacity q_ult = 5.14 c_u (undrained, Prandtl), clay consistency (very soft c_u < 12 kPa), void ratio/porosity relations
TERZAGHI.lic: book, copyright; formulas and class limits used as facts

LEKNER88.cite: Lekner J, Dorf MC. Why some things are darker when wet. Appl Opt 27:1278-1280 (1988); Twomey SA, Bohren CF, Mergenthaler JL. Reflectance and albedo differences between wet and dry surfaces. Appl Opt 25:431 (1986)
LEKNER88.lic: paywalled; the mechanism (total internal reflection in the water film, more absorption per photon path) used as fact

LOBELL02.cite: Lobell DB, Asner GP. Moisture effects on soil reflectance. Soil Sci Soc Am J 66:722-727 (2002). Recalled: reflectance falls roughly exponentially with water content, most of the drop in the first ~0.1-0.2 v/v

FAROUKI81.cite: Farouki OT. Thermal Properties of Soils. CRREL Monograph 81-1, US Army Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (1981)

LEJEUNE98.cite: Lejeune TM, Willems PA, Heglund NC. Mechanics and energetics of human locomotion on sand. J Exp Biol 201:2071-2080 (1998). Recalled: walking on sand costs 1.6-2.5x firm ground, running 1.2-1.6x
LEJEUNE98.lic: free to read (JEB archive); numbers used as facts

MALITSON_QZ.cite: Quartz ordinary index n_o ~1.544 at 589 nm (Ghosh 1999 via refractiveindex.info)

ANON_E.cite: Estimate made in this lane; the reason is given in each src
